questions.question: Is a color combination that passes WCAG contrast still comfortable to look at?
questions.answer_summary: No — WCAG's 4.5:1 ratio is a binary pass/fail check that doesn't capture perceptual eye strain; a follow-up 'color comfort score' concept was proposed after this gap was raised on Hacker News.

questions.question: What is APCA and how does it differ from WCAG 2.x contrast math?
questions.answer_summary: APCA (Advanced Perceptual Contrast Algorithm) is discussed as a likely successor to WCAG's flat contrast ratio, since it also factors in font size/weight and perceptual luminance rather than a single ratio number.

questions.question: What contrast ratio do I need to hit WCAG AA vs AAA?
questions.answer_summary: Normal text needs 4.5:1 (AA) or 7:1 (AAA); large text (14pt bold+/18pt+) needs 3:1 (AA) or 4.5:1 (AAA); UI components/graphics need at least 3:1 under WCAG 2.1 AA.

questions.question: Is there a Mac app that checks a color palette for WCAG/accessibility compliance?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — 'Clarity,' a macOS app specifically for checking color accessibility and WCAG compliance, was shown on Hacker News as a Show HN launch.

questions.question: Can I test a whole palette's pairings against real components at once instead of one pair at a time?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — tools like Paletra let you build a palette and test it against WCAG thresholds across UI components in one pass rather than checking foreground/background pairs individually.

questions.question: Are there AI tools that generate large batches of curated color palettes for designers?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — Palettepoint (120K+ curated palettes) and Palettt both market themselves as AI-powered palette generators aimed at designers, shown as recent Show HN launches.

questions.question: Does color accessibility testing need to cover colorblindness, not just light/dark contrast?
questions.answer_summary: Yes — some dedicated color tools (e.g. IRIX color scheme editor) explicitly test contrast ratio, lightness, and color-blindness issues together rather than contrast alone.

questions.question: How do I quickly check one color pair for accessibility without a design tool?
questions.answer_summary: WebAIM's free Contrast Checker lets you enter hex values or use an eyedropper to sample on-screen colors and instantly see a pass/fail against AA/AAA thresholds.

questions.question: Why do indie developers keep building new AI color-palette generators?
questions.answer_summary: Hacker News' Show HN section shows repeated recent launches (Gradienty, Palettepoint, Palettt, Hexee Pro, colorpal), suggesting sustained builder interest in AI-assisted palette generation as a recurring project niche, though this is builder-side evidence rather than proof of large end-user search demand.
